hops.title: Point at it: baby ladybugs on garden leaves
hops.text: On a walk through a yard or park, stop by leafy garden plants and hunt for ladybug babies together. Many ladybug larvae look like tiny spiny black-and-orange alligators with six legs, nothing like the round spotted adults. Stay close, look with eyes only, and never touch unknown bugs.

sources.citation: University of California Statewide IPM Program (UC ANR), 'Lady Beetles'

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A parent and child seen from behind looking closely at a green leaf holding both a tiny spiky black-and-orange ladybug larva and a round red spotted ladybug.
image.caption: Many baby ladybugs look like tiny spiny alligators before they become round beetles.

hops.title: Say it: welcome to the biggest club on Earth
hops.text: When your first beetle climbs out, try cheering, "Welcome to the biggest club on Earth!" Then tell your child why: scientists have named more than 380,000 kinds of beetles, about one in every four kinds of animals anyone has named. That little tub beetle has an enormous family.

sources.citation: Zhang et al. (2018), 'Evolutionary history of Coleoptera revealed by extensive sampling of genes and species', Nature Communications (via PMC / NIH)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A shiny dark mealworm beetle standing on rolled oats next to several other beetles of different colors and shapes.
image.caption: About one in every four kinds of named animals on Earth is a beetle.

hops.title: Compare it: a bigger coat under a tight sweater
hops.text: After your child guesses where a thin, empty skin came from, try this: could you pull on a bigger winter coat underneath a tight sweater? A mealworm does just that. Its hard outside cannot stretch, so it builds a soft new one inside, splits the old one and crawls out, often around 15 times.

sources.citation: North Carolina State University, ENT 425 General Entomology, 'Morphogenesis'
Arizona State University School of Life Sciences, Ask A Biologist, 'Beetle Life Cycle'

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A snug sweater beside a larger winter coat on a bench next to a tray where a pale mealworm crawls out of its thin empty shed skin.
image.caption: To grow, a mealworm builds a roomier soft shell inside its old one and crawls out.
